text:
support_esc: Customer Ops (large SaaS) reporting widespread 502/504 + timeouts to hosted inference endpoints in eu-west-1 starting ~09:05 UTC. They see SDK retries and high latency. They've opened an escalation.
sarah: I can repro from my laptop via eu-west-1: curl to /v1/generate returns 502 consistently. Here's a sample:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml-13b","prompt":"hi"}'
> HTTP/2 502\n< server: envoy\n< x-request-id: ...\n```
support_esc: Also getting multiple customers now, some on different clouds. Support queue spiking.
monitoring-bot: ALERT gateway-5xx-rate: eu-west-1 > 6.2% (5m avg)\nALERT tcp-conn-reset-rate: eu-west-1-gateway > 4.1%
mike: Netops - starting network checks. Can someone run mtr/traceroute to the gateway IPs from affected hosts? I want to see where packet loss occurs.
sean: Running mtr from our client-sim infra in us-east to eu-west gateway: shows ~25-40% loss at a hop labeled "transit-isp-1". Subsequent hops show recovery but higher RTTs. attaching mtr output snippet:
```
HOST: client-sim\n 1.|-- isp-peering-1 0.6%\n 2.|-- transit-isp-1 32.7%\n 3.|-- transit-isp-1-bgp 31.1%\n 4.|-- aws-nlb-eu-west 5.3%\n```
raj: I see similar from our synthetic agents inside eu-west-1 AZ-b: packet loss between AZ-b->gateway-ngw is spiky. tcpdump on gateway shows lots of retransmits and RSTs when loss peaks. tcpdump snippet:
```
09:06:12.123 IP x.x.x.x.34234 > y.y.y.y.443: Flags [P.], seq 1234:1300, ack 4567, win 64240\n09:06:12.124 IP y.y.y.y.443 > x.x.x.x.34234: RST\n```
netops-bot: Creating provider ticket with transit-isp-1 (ref: TICKET-92411). Escalation to NOC on-call.
mike: Provider acknowledged potential BGP flap / route churn around 09:02-09:08 UTC affecting several prefixes. They say they're validating filters. Can we activate failover routing now to eu-central-1 for hosted-api traffic for affected customer segments?
julia: We have a traffic-shift playbook. I'm starting a canary shift for 10% traffic for non-sso customers -> eu-central-1 via our smart-routing policy. Rolling now: set route weight eu-west-1=90 -> eu-central-1=10.
sarah: Support: drafted status update for customers. Need approval to include "possible transit provider networking issue causing intermittent 5xxs in eu-west-1".
support_esc: Approve, include mitigation steps and suggestion to retry. Also add note: billing: some customers ask that retries during incident are non-billable — we should coordinate with billing.
monitoring-bot: NOTE gateway-5xx-rate: eu-west-1 dropped to 3.1% after initial traffic shift (10%)
sean: After shifting 25% traffic, our synthetic tests show fewer 502s but some requests still high-latency (p95 ~ 1.2s -> 2.8s). Possibly cross-AZ buffering/backpressure. Need to check NLB and target health.
raj: Checking NLB target groups: some backend instances in AZ-b show unhealthy due to TCP healthcheck failures. Marking targets draining and moving traffic to healthy targets in AZ-a and AZ-c.
mike: Provider confirmed they applied a community filter and withdrew a bad path. They reported BGP convergence finishing at 09:18 UTC. They claim packet loss should be reduced. Monitoring — please verify.
sean: Running mtr now shows transit-isp-1 loss down to 2-3%. p95 latency normalized. Gateway 5xx rate trending to baseline.
support_esc: Customer Ops confirmed degraded behavior is resolved on their end. They asked for RCA and whether we can credit retry charges for the window 09:02-09:20 UTC.
julia: I'll draft incident timeline and start a postmortem. Action items: (1) update routing policy to auto-failover to eu-central when packet loss > 10% for 3m, (2) improve our canary weight ramping to 50% within 5m, (3) add provider BGP monitoring for prefix flaps, (4) review billing credits policy for incident retries.
mike: Short-term: enable stricter NLB healthchecks and reduce time-to-drain to speed AZ failover. Also recommend adding per-AZ ingress endpoints so cross-AZ transit is avoided where possible.
netops-bot: Provider ticket updated: TICKET-92411 -> root cause: transit provider BGP misconfiguration on their edge causing intermittent packet loss across our prefixes. Mitigation applied by provider filter 09:15 UTC. Close pending confirmation.
sarah: Support to customer: sent post-incident note and offered 10% service credit + B2B billing review if retries billed. Customer responded :thumbsup: asked for postmortem.
monitoring-bot: FINAL: gateway-5xx-rate eu-west-1 back to 0.8% (1h avg). All monitors green.
support_esc: Closing this thread. Postmortem owner: julia, target publish by EOD tomorrow. Follow-ups: engineering to add automated routing fallback and billing to review credits for impacted customers.
julia: Adding runbook item: during provider BGP events, escalate to provider NOC and consider immediate multi-region traffic shift. Also add command snippets for quick mtr/tcpdump checks.
sean: Putting links into the postmortem: dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/gateway-eu-west-1, provider ticket: https://transit-isp.status/tickets/92411
support_esc: Thanks team. I'll update the customers in the escalations queue with the resolution and link to the postmortem when published.
